kjv: Why are thy valiant [men] swept away? they stood not
mine: Why has Apis fled? Why does your bull not stand?
note: MT nischaph 'abbireka "your mighty one is swept away"; the LXX redivides as nas chaph "Hapi (Apis) has fled", with 'abbir "bull" referring to the Apis bull of Memphis (v. 14). I follow the LXX division.

kjv: destruction cometh; it cometh out of the north
mine: a gadfly from the north has come upon her
note: Hebrew qerets (hapax) is best understood as a stinging insect (gadfly) that torments the "beautiful heifer" Egypt; "destruction" loses the image.
Hebrew 'amon minno' is "Amon of No (Thebes)", the chief Egyptian god Amun; the KJV takes 'amon as hamon "multitude", hiding the reference to Egypt's god alongside "her gods".
